rule: The onboarding client is the script named OnboardingClient. Its tables copy, pages, resolvers, pageSignals, placement, actionSteps and pageOrder are read by name. A target is a call inside a resolver or page signal that passes a string literal to a local helper; `match_on` is what that helper (and the helpers it calls) compares: instance Name, Text, a child of PlayerGui, or attributes.

MobileDriving.signal_source: function() local object=UserInputService.TouchEnabled and (named("DriftLeft") or named("DriftLeftButton")); return object and scopeRoot(object) end

VehicleShortcut.signal_source: function() local object=state.Stage>=2 and named("Car"); return object and scopeRoot(object) end

RaceShortcut.signal_source: function() local object=state.SeenPages.GarageShortcut==true and named("Race"); return object and scopeRoot(object) end

EventMode.signal_source: function() local root=screenRoot("RaceEntryPresentation"); return root and buttonWithText("TIME TRIAL",root) and buttonWithText("RACE",root) and root end

TimeTrialSetup.signal_source: function() local object=named("TierE"); local root=scopeRoot(object); return root and named("LapSelector",root) and root end

RaceSetup.signal_source: function() local object=named("RaceFormat"); return object and scopeRoot(object) end

GarageShortcut.signal_source: function() local object=state.SeenPages.VehicleShortcut==true and named("Garage"); return object and scopeRoot(object) end

G1.copy: Vehicle categories group cars into families. Cars in the same category can share compatible modules.

G4.copy: Tier shows the vehicle's performance class. Overall rating gives a quick summary of its total performance.

A2.copy: You have limited vehicle space. Buy more garages to increase your capacity.

G2.copy: Select a vehicle to preview it. Buy it to add it to your collection.

J1.copy: Buy and equip modules in each vehicle slot. Modules can be swapped between vehicles in the same category.

J2.copy: Upgrade the modules fitted to your vehicle. Each module has several upgrade paths and a limited point budget.

J3.copy: Change your vehicle's paint and lighting per module. You can also customise thrust, neon and underglow.

K1.copy: Choose a module location. Buy and swap modules from your different owned vehicles.

L1.copy: Choose an equipped module to see its upgrades. Different modules offer different upgrade paths.

L2.copy: Each module has a limited upgrade-point budget. Spending points on one upgrade leaves fewer for the others.

M1.copy: Choose which part of the vehicle you want to customise. You can edit the whole vehicle, cockpit, effects or individual modules.

D7.copy: Use the drift arrows while turning to slide around corners. Drifting helps with tighter turns.

D8.copy: Hold Boost for a burst of speed. The boost meter shows how much energy remains.

B2.copy: Open My Vehicles to spawn, switch or despawn your cars. New vehicles appear here after you buy them.

B4.copy: Open the Race Browser to find events around the city. Events can support races, time trials or both.

N1.copy: Select an event to view its route and details.

N6.copy: Teleport to the selected event's starting area.

O1.copy: Choose Race to compete against other players. Choose Time Trial to race against target times.

Q1.copy: Choose a vehicle class for the time trial. Each class has separate target times, records and eligible vehicles.

Q5.copy: This shows your selected class and the best available reward. Higher tiers have greater rewards.

Q8.copy: Beat these target times to earn medals and cash. Faster times award higher medals.

Q4.copy: Choose how many timed laps you want to run. Your best completed lap is used for the result.

P1.copy: This shows the route, lap count and player limit. Multiplayer races use an open vehicle category.
P1.resolver_source: function(root) return group(root,"RaceFormat") or group(root,"DetailColumn") end

B3.copy: Open My Garages to view your owned properties. Each garage can display vehicles and has its own customisation.

X1.copy: Choose one of your owned garage properties. Each card shows how many display spaces it contains.

X3.copy: Enter the selected garage. You can manage its vehicles, assets and appearance from inside.

Z1.copy: Choose which owned vehicles are displayed in your garage. Each vehicle is assigned to a physical display space.

Z2.copy: Buy and equip different walls, floors, ceilings, decorations and lighting.

Z3.copy: Customise the assets already equipped in your garage. Change their colours, materials and lighting.

AA1.copy: Choose a display space to manage. Empty spaces can receive a vehicle, while occupied spaces can be changed.

AB1.copy: Choose Structure, Decorations or Lighting. Build adds new assets; Style changes the look of equipped assets.

AC1.copy: Choose which section of the garage you want to rebuild. The selected style is previewed in that location.

AD1.copy: Choose where you want to place a decoration. Each location has its own compatible asset options.
